## Overview

My research focuses on quantifying and understanding CO<sub>2</sub> fluxes across the atmosphere-biosphere-ocean system, combining satellite remote sensing with inverse modeling techniques.

### Remote Sensing & Inversion of CO2 Fluxes

I use satellite-derived trace gas retrievals together with atmospheric transport and inversion frameworks to estimate surface CO<sub>2</sub> fluxes and constrain their spatial and temporal distribution.

*Add details: instruments/datasets used (e.g., OCO-2, OCO-3, GOSAT, TROPOMI), inversion frameworks, and key findings.*

### Carbon Cycle Processes

Investigating the drivers of terrestrial and oceanic carbon uptake and release, and how these processes respond to climate variability.

### Greenhouse Gas Dynamics at Regional Scales

Studying the regional-scale distribution and variability of CO<sub>2</sub>, CH<sub>4</sub>, and N<sub>2</sub>O, and their links to land-use, emissions, and natural sink/source processes.

### Carbon-Climate Interactions & Global Warming

Examining feedbacks between the carbon cycle and the climate system, and how these interactions shape projections of future warming.
